sources.entry: WebHook Tester - Powerful tool for testing WebHooks and more. MIT Docker/Go/deb/K8S

summary.one_liner: A self-hosted webhook and HTTP request testing tool that generates unique URLs, records incoming requests, and lets you customize the responses, with a ReactJS UI compiled into a Go binary.
summary.what_it_does: WebHook Tester gives you randomly generated URLs that capture incoming webhooks and HTTP requests, and shows them in a built-in web UI. You can set the response status code, Content-Type header, response body, and a response delay. The Go binary embeds the ReactJS frontend, so no extra assets are needed. WebSocket support pushes new requests to the UI in real time. Storage can be in memory, Redis, or the local filesystem, and pub/sub can be memory or Redis. An optional ngrok tunnel driver exposes a local instance to the internet. The app also provides a /healthz endpoint and a CLI health check subcommand.
use_cases: Debug and inspect incoming webhooks from third-party services
Test HTTP client requests and see exactly what was sent
Receive GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket webhooks on a local machine via ngrok tunnel
Simulate endpoints with custom status codes, headers and delayed responses
Run a webhook capture service on Kubernetes with Helm
how_to_run: Alternatively, download the release binary for your OS and architecture and run: ./webhook-tester start
Kubernetes: install the Helm chart from ArtifactHUB
notable: Single binary with the React UI embedded, no extra assets needed
Three storage drivers: memory, Redis, and fs, selected with --storage-driver
Auto-create sessions for requests that carry a UUID-formatted prefix
Built-in ngrok tunnel driver that starts without installing ngrok separately
Multi-architecture Docker image that runs as an unprivileged user
caveats: The public demo at wh.tarampamp.am is limited, does not persist data, and may be unavailable
Tunneling requires an ngrok auth token
Multiple app instances need the Redis pub/sub driver and, for shared data, Redis storage
keywords: see what a service sent me
